job: JOB 35: Weathering of base and walls (moss and cracks at the ground, light wear above)
why: Moss and cracked-stone patches now sit on the plinth and base corners in believable clusters, adding the aged ground-level finish the concept shows, without altering the silhouette or clutter above.

job: JOB 32: Mossy plinth base course (stair foot, two courses, moss gradient)
why: The after view adds a dark stepped stone-brick plinth around the base that grounds the building and better matches the concept's plinth, though the mossy gradient is mostly lost and the foot reads somewhat heavy and uniform.

job: JOB 33: Flagstone pavement border around the front
why: The lighter flagstone border around the front base adds a visible paved edge like the concept's stone plinth, with a subtle texture change and no silhouette damage or clutter.

job: JOB 1: INSPECTORATE plaque (stone tablet proud of the frieze, dark lettering row, chiselled end bosses)
why: The pale stone tablet with dark lettering blocks and corner bosses sits proud of the frieze, as the concept's INSPECTORATE plaque does. It adds depth and a focal point, though the lettering is only crude dark blocks and the tablet cuts slightly into the neighbouring timber column.

job: JOB 2: PERMIT OFFICE fascia sign (quartz plate, gold lettering band, light-blue end caps)
why: The white fascia sign with light-blue end caps and gold lettering blocks now sits over the entrance, matching the concept's PERMIT OFFICE sign placement and palette, though the gold blocks are only abstract dashes without letter shapes and the caps are a bit saturated.

job: JOB 3: Pediment raking cornice (stepped stair line picked out in polished andesite, foot blocks)
why: The raking cornice now picks out the pediment's stepped edge in lighter polished andesite with corner foot blocks, which gives the gable a defined profile and depth that matches the concept's stepped pediment, with no clutter or colour clash.

job: JOB 4: Gold cross emblem in the pediment tympanum
why: The gold cross fills the previously blank pediment tympanum as in the concept, but it is blocky and slightly oversized with an irregular stepped shape, so it's a modest gain.

job: JOB 5: Roof pinnacles: mossy bases, stone caps in place of the fires
why: The glowing fires on the roof pinnacles are replaced with stone-capped tops and a little moss, which fits the weathered stone look of the concept's finials, and the silhouette stays clean with no clutter.

job: JOB 6: Vertical timber piers: widen the piers beside the windows to two blocks
why: The widened piers render as pale, flat light-oak blocks with a ragged stepped edge on the right pier, which breaks the clean timber columns and clashes with the darker, weathered tone in the concept.

job: JOB 7: Pier capitals (upside-down oak stairs on each pier head)
why: The upside-down oak stair capitals add a small flared head to each wooden pier, giving the column a visible capital profile that the concept shows (columns meeting the entablature) without disturbing the silhouette, colour or surrounding detailing.

job: JOB 8: Corbel row under the eave (trapdoors in the recessed gaps of the dentil frieze)
why: The corbel row adds only faint, barely visible dark slivers under the eave line, so there is no real gain in depth or finish and no visible damage to the silhouette.

job: JOB 9: Eave cornice (stepped stone lip, full width, returning round the sides)
why: The stepped stone lip now projects with a visible profile and shadow and returns round the side and front, adding depth and a crafted cornice line under the roof like the concept, with no colour clash or broken silhouette.

job: JOB 10: Upper-storey windows: transom bar across the dark glass
why: Small amber mullion bars now break up the flat dark glass in the upper-storey windows, adding the transom detail the concept shows without disturbing the silhouette or colours, though they're sparse and slightly thin.

job: JOB 11: Dark jambs: banded polished deepslate and tiles at each window side, tiled centre pier
why: The before and after close-ups are nearly identical; the dark window jambs and tiled centre pier are barely visible at this scale, so the change adds no visible crafted detail and does no harm.

job: JOB 12: Window hoods (stone-brick stairs over every upper window)
why: The stone-brick stair hoods add a subtle projecting lintel over each upper window in both elevations, giving depth and a finished profile like the concept's heavy window surrounds without clutter or colour clash.

job: JOB 13: Window sills with flower boxes
why: Small flower boxes with sills now sit under each upper-storey window on both elevations, which matches the concept's window-box detail and adds colour and depth without disturbing the silhouette, though the blooms are small and slightly dark-on-dark.

job: JOB 14: Closed wooden shutters on the right-most window, front and side
why: The 'shutters' render as two thin vertical brown slats running the full window height, which don't read as closed shutters and leave the opening dark and empty, so it looks like noise rather than a crafted detail.

job: JOB 15: Hanging lanterns beside the corner piers
why: The small lanterns hung at the corner piers match the concept's hanging lanterns and add a bit of detail, but they are tiny, barely visible at this scale, and one reads as a slightly floating or stray block at the right edge, so the build doesn't gain much.

job: JOB 16: Slim mossy pilasters with gold caps beside the corner piers
why: The slim mossy pilasters with gold caps add only a few small pixels at the outer corners, and the gold caps read as slightly odd yellow blocks, so the build is barely changed.

job: JOB 17: Chiselled corner bosses above the string course
why: The chiselled corner bosses add small stone-block accents at the string-course corners on the front elevation, echoing the concept's corner blocks and breaking up the flat band without harming the silhouette or colours.

job: JOB 18: String course between the storeys
why: The after view adds a continuous grey stone string course (with a small projecting lip) at the storey break, which separates the dark upper floor from the white lower floor and matches the concept's banding, with no damage to the silhouette or windows.

job: JOB 19: Stepped arch heads over the shopfront bays
why: The arch heads over the shopfront bays are barely visible: a small grey block above the centre door and slight changes over the side bays. They don't give the stepped-arch profile the concept shows, and they add no clutter or colour error.

job: JOB 20: Shopfront glazing with a light-blue mullion grid
why: The after view shows a tidier light-blue mullion grid, with a clearer central glazed entry bay and side windows that read as shopfront glass, closer to the concept's pale-blue mullioned storefront, though the change is subtle.

job: JOB 21: Wall-mounted bracket lanterns on the ground-floor piers
why: Small dark-iron bracket lanterns on the ground-floor piers add the lit, hanging-lantern detail the concept shows, in a fitting colour and placement, though one lantern on the right looks slightly offset.

job: JOB 22: Hanging lanterns inside the arcade bays
why: Small lanterns now hang inside the arcade bays and over the door, matching the concept's warm interior lanterns, while the silhouette and the colours stay intact and the added detail is restrained.

job: JOB 23: Soul lantern on a bracket left of the entrance
why: The second bracket and cyan soul lantern sit on a different level and are offset from the existing warm lantern, so they read as a duplicated, cluttered pair, and the cyan clashes with the warm lantern palette; the concept has just one orange lantern per pier.

job: JOB 24: Teal banners at the ground-floor corners (concrete panels with a gold cross)
why: The teal banners with a gold stripe sit at the ground-floor corners, as the concept shows, and add accent colour that echoes the teal trim on the Permit Office sign. They read as flat colour slabs with no cross, hang slightly proud of the corner, and are slightly oversaturated, but they don't break the silhouette.

job: JOB 25: Copper rods beside the corner banners
why: The thin copper rods beside the corner banners are barely visible, add only a tiny amount of detail that matches the concept's copper accents, and neither clutter nor break the silhouette.

job: JOB 26: Entrance doors: dark timber surround and gold keystone
why: The door surround darkens from mid-brown to near-black dark oak, which better matches the concept's dark timber frame, but the gold keystone is not visible and the change is subtle, so the entrance looks only marginally different.

job: JOB 27: Entrance steps: nosed treads and side cheeks
why: The change opens a see-through hole in the bottom step course and a gap beside the cheek, creating broken voids and a ragged silhouette instead of crisp nosed treads and cheeks like the concept's clean white entrance stairs.

job: JOB 28: Planters with white flowers flanking the bays and the entrance
why: Small planters with pink-white blooms now sit flanking the bays and entrance at the base, adding a concept-matching ground-level detail in a believable scale without disturbing the silhouette, though the flowers read slightly pink rather than white.

job: JOB 29: Filing cabinet with scattered papers right of the steps
why: A small dark wood filing cabinet with scattered paper bits beside the steps adds the storytelling prop the concept shows, at the right scale and tone, with no silhouette break, though it is tiny and slightly merges with the planter barrels in the close-ups.

job: JOB 30: Shop counters seen through the glass
why: Dark wooden counters now sit behind the left and right shop windows, replacing the pale tan blocks and giving the glazing some interior depth like the concept's desks, though they are small and slightly stark.

job: JOB 31: Dark timber colonnade posts on the side return
why: The flat near-black posts stick out of the side return as a bare slab, with unfinished gaps at the base and the lantern and banner partly hidden, rather than reading as a crafted colonnade like the concept's brown timber columns.

job: JOB 36: Roof edge coping
why: The coping adds small stone caps atop the corner chimneys and a slightly stepped roof edge, giving a more finished profile with no colour clash and no silhouette damage.

job: JOB 37: Side-return belt: window frames on the ground-floor arcade
why: The before and after side-return arcades look nearly identical; any added window frames are too subtle to read at this close-up and don't change the silhouette or colour.

job: JOB 34: Chimney with copper pot on the rear west roof
why: The new chimney is a wide, detached block floating off the roof slope (visible gap beneath it in the right elevation) with a bright orange copper cap that doesn't match the dark slate palette, and it leaves the old thin chimney standing beside it, so the silhouette gets cluttered and broken.
